name: Oren Pinkham
equipment: Heavy coat: a keeper's double-breasted wool reefer, thirty years old and darned at both elbows by a wife who has been dead for six
Lever-action rifle (a .30 Winchester he uses on sea ducks, seals that rob the weirs and, once in 1909, a rabid dog), 10 in the magazine
Hatchet, for kindling, ice on the gallery rail and the frozen fog-bell machinery
The keys of Carrow Head Light Station, and the station's logbooks, 1857 to 1924, on a shelf in the watch room; his father's volume for 1871 is wrapped in oilcloth at the back
A twelve-foot ducking punt and a double-ended peapod with oars, at the Head's boat slip
A brass telescope, a barometer he trusts more than God, and a tide table annotated in three colors of ink
A pipe, a pouch of Union Leader tobacco, and a coffee pot that is never quite empty
features: Something to Hold On To (Faithful origin: once per long rest, when gaining Dread, gain 1 fewer; advantage on saves against being charmed or compelled by a creature; no miracle in it, only staying yourself). He holds on by doing his duty aloud: winding the fog bell, trimming the lamp, writing the log

Know Your Quarry (Hunter: after an hour studying a creature's sign, wet tracks on a stair, a pattern in the logbook, he declares it his quarry: advantage on Survival checks to track it and Perception checks to find it, he always knows which way it went from where he found its sign, and once on each of his turns a weapon hit on it deals an extra 1d6, applied at the table and not written on the sheet)

Fieldcraft (Hunter: he can't become lost on the island or on water he has crossed except by something not natural, moves at normal pace while moving stealthily outdoors, and in a short rest can rig a tripwire bell that warns him of anything within 30 ft)

Cold Focus (Hunter, 2nd level: when he fails a fear check against his quarry he still gains the Dread but has advantage on his next attack against it; when he succeeds he can move half his speed without provoking opportunity attacks)
Way of the Hunt: Hunter of the Uncanny (Hunter, 3rd level: once he has declared a supernatural creature his quarry, the GM tells him one of its rules about what hurts it or bars it)

Keeper's Log (Lighthouse Keeper background: reads the weather and the sea a day ahead without a check, knows every lamp, lens and fog signal, is welcomed by keepers and fishermen on any coast, and has advantage on the first fear check each night that he makes while alone)

personality.traits: I write it down. Weather, wind, vessels passing, oil used, what the bell did. I say grace at every meal including a cup of coffee. I laugh at my own jokes before I get to the end of them.
personality.ideals: A logbook is the truth, because nobody but the inspector ever reads it. My father taught me that, and he wrote one page I wish to God he had not had to.
personality.bonds: Carrow Head Light, which my father kept for twenty-nine years and I have kept for twenty-seven. My wife Abbie's grave on Spruce Hill. The island, which is not mine: a Pinkham is from away until the third generation, and I am the second.
personality.flaws: I have known since 1890 what my father's log says about the night of 18 October 1871, and I have never shown it to anyone, because my father told me it was not ours to tell. I keep telling myself it still isn't. It is cowardice, and I know it.

appearance: A short, round, red-faced man of sixty-one with a white fringe of hair, bright blue eyes in a web of weather wrinkles, a pipe in the corner of his mouth, and big hands black with kerosene soot. Keeper's reefer, cap with the Lighthouse Service badge, gum boots, a pencil behind his ear.
backstory: Oren Pinkham was born at Carrow Head Light in 1863, the son of the keeper, Nehemiah Pinkham, who came from Cape Elizabeth to keep it in 1868 and kept it until he died in 1897, when Oren, his assistant for ten years, took over. He married an island woman, Abbie Farr, who died in 1918 of the influenza; they had no family. He is not of the five families by blood; his wife was. He has been on Carrow fifty-six years and is still, to the island, the keeper's son from away, which suits him. He keeps the light perfectly, has saved eleven lives from wrecks off the Head, and knows the tides, the ledges and the sky better than anyone alive except Galen Coombs. In 1924 he has heard the drowned bell five times and written down every one, with the time of low water beside it, because a keeper logs what he hears. The fifth time, 30 September, Ellery Wyman asked him to set the fog bell's clockwork going through the low water, and he did, and it did no good, and he wrote that down too.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Oren is the party's anchor at the Head and the keeper of the campaign's key clue. He joins whoever earns his trust, starting with Jonas Weatherby, his new assistant, whom he likes on sight because Jonas does not talk. His 1924 log is CLUE A1 and his father's 1871 log is CLUE D1; he shows the first readily and the second only when he has decided that the party will do right by it, or when the GM needs it shown (see controlFile.theKeyClue: he puts it on the table and says nothing). In db-scenario-002 he works out the hundred-year tide from the almanac, the perigee and the barometer, and tells the party the hour; he can row or pole them across the Bar's channels in the dark. In the storm his iron tower is the island's one sure refuge (CLUE E4), and when the light goes out it is his to relight. He is a fine shot and a patient tracker, slow on his feet.
dmNotes.voice: Down East to the bone: 'ayuh', 'some wicked', 'from away', 'it's coming on thick'. Slow and warm, full of weather and bad jokes, every sentence ending on a downturn. Says 'Mother' when he means his late wife. Goes completely flat and quiet when he talks about his father's log.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: keep the light, and keep the people on the water alive. Secondary: let his father's page do some good at last. Tertiary: live to see the bell stop, so that he can write in the log 'bell not heard', and close it.
dmNotes.secrets: His father told him in 1890 what the page means: that Nehemiah Pinkham watched the five lanterns on the Bar through the station telescope for four hours, could have launched the station boat and did not, because he was a federal keeper from away and the island's selectmen had posted a watch and told him the fever was in there. Nehemiah never forgave himself. Oren's second secret: his wife Abbie was a Farr, and on the night of 1 August, when Enoch Farr walked into the sea, Oren heard his own wife's maiden name in the bell, six years after her death.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: hospitable from the first cup of coffee, guarded about the past. Toward Jonas: fatherly at once. Toward Ellery Wyman: old neighbourly respect and a growing anger. Toward Galen Coombs: he logs Galen's boats going out without lights and has never once reported them. Toward Orpha Sprague: deep courtesy; they are the two people on Carrow who know.
